correctness.rationale: For distinct uncovered vertices, the symmetric difference is exactly the unique even alternating tree path; consecutive path exchanges yield distance equal to half input-tree distance, and each flip can move the uncovered vertex by at most two edges. The D/A edge saturation argument forces the induced exposure core to be the once-subdivision of a unique tree. All remaining components have forced internal perfect matchings attached only to subdivision vertices. The explicit converse realizes every finite tree. Exhaustive labelled tree tests through order seven and deterministic larger tests replay the full stated algorithm but do not replace the unlimited-order proof.

originality.rationale: The tree-specific canonical exposed-vertex core and full isomorphism/realization of the one-hole matching flip graph were not located in inspected primary texts. The cardinality/equality theorem for once-subdivided trees is Cambie et al. (2025); in addition, Bousquet et al. (2018) observe that no reconfiguration detour is required for matchings whose line graph is even-hole-free, which includes forests. Thus the exact tree distance formula is a classical consequence and is not asserted independently as a novel formula. The potentially new result is the complete forced-fringe core and flip-graph classification, with historical priority provisional.

value.rationale: Natural complete structural classification of reconfiguration graphs arising from all odd-order trees with one-hole matchings. The exact metric and forced-fringe decomposition are useful for computing radii, diameters and distance distributions and explain which tree shapes occur. The converse realizes every finite tree, a substantive characterization rather than an isolated small computation or the known bound on matching counts.
